findings: ADOPT (adopt-design): Exact additive patch financial-report.patch (sha256 03f868a9702c456fe2992c9268f75d43e2bd6ae61db9c5c5be4cef632ead03fc) is suitable for adoption as an observational report-contract design extension for accepted finite Rust moriarty/1 / moriarty-core/1 Transfer, Fee, Liability, and Discharge statements. Because the patch text itself carries explicit '(unadopted)' headings and self-limiting status clauses ('Its SHALL clauses remain unadopted until a separately recorded design decision', 'The financial observation extension SHALL remain design-only until independently adopted'), explicit recorded adoption is required before these SHALL clauses become the active effective contract.

Baseline preservation verified: financial-report.patch is strictly additive across docs/CORE-EXECUTION-REPORTS.md (inserting 35 lines immediately before '## Provenance and conformance') and openspec/changes/consolidated-language-kernel/specs/consolidated-language-kernel/spec.md (inserting one child paragraph each at the end of UNI-018, UNI-020, and UNI-021). Zero baseline lines are deleted or modified; NR-01 through NR-06, the Counter and empty-action specifications, the logical-work schedule, the 28,093-byte mori test normal Transfer aggregate compatibility clause, and the relative Markdown link '../../../../../docs/CORE-EXECUTION-REPORTS.md#proposed-financial-observation-extension-unadopted' are preserved intact.

Statement ExprId vs outer typed Step.value vs Effect field representation verified against baseline/crates/mori-core/src/ir.rs (lines 12-52, 104-270, 278-360), parser.rs (lines 355-358), and runtime.rs (lines 488-498, 758-862): (1) Step.statement serializes with tag 'kind' and retains exact admitted IR fields where amount is an ExprId (u16 zero-based index into Program.expressions) and asset (for Transfer, Fee, Liability) is the declared asset alias String; (2) outer Step.value is always Some(Value::UInt(amount)), serializing as {"type":"UInt","value":"<q>"} with q as a canonical unsigned decimal string (including "0") representing the moved, charged, added, or discharged amount rather than an ExprId, boolean, recipient balance, closing duty amount, null, or omitted field; (3) Step.effects elements use full AssetId {network, issuer, reference, scale} and bare UInt canonical decimal strings for amount, before, and after without a typed Value wrapper.

Expression evaluation and frame ordering verified against runtime.rs (lines 417-487, 531-670, 883-917): amount expression q is evaluated immediately before the statement transition against current state, action inputs, prior let captures, and current snapshot liability reads (liability_present returning Bool(row.is_some()) and liability_amount returning UInt(row.map_or(0, |l| l.amount))). Each Step.snapshot equals complete post-statement S[i] with state (declared states only, excluding inputs and let captures, {} when empty), balances sorted by exact (asset, account) with AssetId ordered by (network, issuer, reference, scale), and liabilities sorted by name ([] when empty), preserving untouched observer balances and incoming external duties.

Zero/self effects and absent vs present-zero duty distinctions verified against runtime.rs (lines 671-703, 758-861): (1) admitted self-transfer and self-fee (from == to after checked_sub sufficiency) leave numeric balances unchanged in S[i] while still emitting Effect::Transfer or Effect::Fee with amount q; (2) admitted zero-amount (q == 0) financial statements still emit their corresponding Effect; (3) zero-amount Liability on an absent name inserts a present-zero duty row (before: "0", after: "0") sorted by name, whereas zero or full Discharge (b - q == 0) mutates l.amount in place and retains the present-zero row in S[i].liabilities; (4) Discharge reuses Effect::Liability {name, asset, debtor, creditor, before, after} with the existing row's identity, so a Liability effect with before == "0" (including q == 0 on absent creation, present-zero addition, or present-zero discharge) cannot by itself distinguish absent creation from a present-zero opening duty or discharge without pairing Step.statement and S[i-1].

Delta vs prefix and metered agreement rules verified against runtime.rs (lines 713, 869-918) and README.md (lines 98-128): Step.effects records only the single new effect produced by that financial statement, while Execution.effects is the ordered concatenation of all per-step deltas (including intervening nonfinancial State/Emit effects and duplicate or zero/self effects). Prefix P[i] remains derived notation rather than a wire field, and positive metered execution under moriarty-reference-logical-cost/1 with a sufficient cap retains the identical Execution without adding a per-Step work field.

Missing financial obligations and existing test-scope boundaries preserved: Core/1 has no Mint, Burn, or dedicated accrual construct; Liability addition of an explicit UInt amount q introduces no interest rate, time basis, day-count, compounding, or accrual semantics. Existing crates/mori-core/tests/financial_pair.rs (lines 107-155, which checks pre/post/effects and step index/statement.kind/snapshot/effects but omits raw Step.statement member/ExprId equality and Step.value) and crates/mori/tests/core_test_report.rs (lines 108-125 and 198-248, which exercise the mori test aggregate report consumer rather than ordinary mori simulate stdout bytes) retain their exact scope with no inferred full raw Step or simulate-byte pass. All U0-U7, M1-M17, MC01-MC08, SP01-SP12, G01-G24, ACTUS, DeFi, and composition exits remain open, and no public developer gate is created.

Concrete wording revisions for post-adoption activation (not blocking adoption of exact candidate patch): when a recorded adoption decision promotes this section from an unadopted candidate to an active contract, (1) replace the heading '## Proposed financial observation extension (unadopted)' with '## Financial observation extension' and replace the three OpenSpec lead-ins '**Proposed financial report observations (unadopted).**', '**Proposed financial deltas (unadopted).**', and '**Proposed financial evidence boundary (unadopted).**' (plus the anchor slug) with adopted labels; (2) replace 'Its SHALL clauses remain unadopted until a separately recorded design decision.' and 'The financial observation extension SHALL remain design-only until independently adopted' with the recorded adoption date and decision reference; and (3) optionally clarify in paragraph 3 of the added section that 'Let A be the exact declared AssetId denoted by the statement's asset alias (for Transfer, Fee and Liability; Discharge uses the existing duty row's AssetId, debtor and creditor in S[i-1]).'
limitations: Source-exposed review only: both the packet author and this reviewer inspected pinned baseline implementation sources (ir.rs, parser.rs, runtime.rs, README.md, financial_pair.rs, core_test_report.rs); source agreement is not independent behavior proof or a runtime conformance result.
No runtime, toolchain, build, test, CLI, compiler, SDK, prover, network, or Git commands were executed during this review; all evidence is static inspection of the readonly review packet.

Expectations for full financial Step.statement/ExprIds, outer Step.value, complete post-statement snapshots, per-step deltas, derived prefixes, logical work, and consumer-specific public stdout bytes remain to be independently derived and frozen before authorized conformance execution, without using evaluator output.

This review is restricted to ordinary observational representation and consumer contract design; it makes no judgment on asset conservation, authorization, authentication, circuit/witness soundness, cryptographic proof validity, ledger phase finality, or hostile/security test coverage, which remain with the designated security owner.
Adopting this observation-contract design closes no U0-U7, M1-M17, MC01-MC08, SP01-SP12, or G01-G24 parent requirement and waives no missing Mint, Burn, or dedicated accrual obligation.
